items.headline: Lead: Lock is cleared to start again, and Seattle's final designations are in
paragraphs: Drew Lock has no injury designation for Sunday in Las Vegas. He was limited all week with elbow and oblique injuries, same as last week, and he will make his second straight start with Sam Darnold out.

Darnold is officially out with ribs and quad injuries, along with left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger). Cross practiced on a limited basis on Thursday, but he is out for this one and tracking to return after Seattle's Week 11 bye, when Darnold is targeting a return too.

Seattle is getting three players back: linebacker Uchenna Nwosu, receiver Rashid Shaheed and nose tackle Brandon Pili were all full participants on Friday and carry no designation. Nobody on the Seahawks is questionable or doubtful.
items.takeaway: Lock starts again with no designation, Darnold, Cross, Nelson and Williams are out, and Nwosu, Shaheed and Pili are back with no designation.

items.headline: Injuries: Brown and Stevenson questionable in Munich, Parsons and Jacobs out in Green Bay
paragraphs: Patriots at Lions, Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET in Munich: A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) are both questionable for New England, and the Patriots ruled out running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness), guard Ben Brown (knee) and cornerback Carlton Davis III (knee). For Detroit, receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) are questionable, and center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) are out. Drake Maye practiced fully all week and carries no designation.

Vikings at Packers: Green Bay ruled out edge rusher Micah Parsons, running back Josh Jacobs (broken finger, needs surgery), center Sean Rhyan and tight end Josh Whyle. Linebacker Zaire Franklin is doubtful. Seven more are questionable, including safety Xavier McKinney, a late add on Friday with a foot injury.

49ers at Cowboys: San Francisco lists tackle Trent Williams (shoulder) as questionable after he sat out Friday, along with four cornerbacks and linebacker Dre Greenlaw. Receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) is out; Deebo Samuel is clear. Dallas ruled out tight end Jake Ferguson (knee, ankle) and four others.

Chiefs at Falcons: Kansas City running back Kenneth Walker did not practice Friday with a groin injury and is questionable for Sunday. Atlanta ruled out receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring). Dolphins at Colts: Miami ruled out center Aaron Brewer (concussion) and receiver Jared Wayne (quad), and listed receiver Chris Bell (knee) as doubtful.
items.takeaway: The questionable list that matters: A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson and Amon-Ra St. Brown in Munich, Kenneth Walker in Atlanta, Trent Williams in Dallas — inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the board after the evening refresh, twice. It is the same board as yesterday — generated November 2, still showing Week 8, now eleven days old. The only game with a market board is Bears at Seahawks, played November 2.

So the headline cards are still from a finished game, and they must not be bet. For the record, they read: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. That game is done. Do not bet those cards. The board also still lists Sam Darnold as Seattle's starter — Drew Lock starts on Sunday, with no injury designation.

Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. Balanced is the strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the model's +EV play. Hit Rate is not worse for not being +EV. It is a different job: most likely to win.

Until the board flips, Sunday has no card at all. That is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The board is still the November 2 board, eleven days old, still showing Week 8 — it still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter and knows nothing about Sunday — so Sunday's prices go through Check.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: the hook — the half point that changes everything
paragraphs: The hook is the half point on a spread — the .5 in -2.5 or +6.5. It exists so a bet cannot push. There is no half point in football scoring, so a spread with a hook always has a winner and a loser.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: the Lions are -2.5. If they win by 3, a bet on the Lions wins. If they win by exactly 2, a bet on the Lions loses — the hook is the difference. Now move the line to -3, no hook: a 3-point win is a push and your stake comes back.

That is why the hook is worth real money. Buying off it, or finding a book that offers -2.5 when another has -3, is the same bet at a better price. Before you take either side, run both prices through Check and see what the app says about each.
items.takeaway: The hook is the half point that stops a push — at -2.5 a 3-point win cashes and a 2-point win loses, so the same game at -2.5 instead of -3 is a genuinely better price.

items.headline: The big numbers have not moved since this morning
paragraphs: The board's headline numbers are where they were this morning. The Jaguars are still -10.5 against the Titans, still the week's biggest favorite. The 49ers at Cowboys total is still 55.5, still the week's highest. The Lions are still -2.5 against the Patriots at DraftKings, with the Patriots +3 best available elsewhere.

The public and the money agree on the Lions. VSiN's free DraftKings row for Patriots at Lions shows 80% of the bets and 66% of the handle on Detroit -2.5, and 79% of the bets and 68% of the handle on the Lions moneyline at -148. Tickets and handle on the same side is not a Fade — there is no disagreement to play against. The line has not moved off -2.5, so nothing in the market argues the price is about to change.

If your book's number is different from the ones here, that is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Nothing moved since this morning — Jaguars still -10.5, 49ers-Cowboys total still 55.5, Lions still -2.5 with the public and the money agreeing, which is not a Fade.

items.headline: Tonight's job: know your questionable names, then get your number before the rush
paragraphs: The one thing worth waiting for is inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday. If your bet depends on A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Kenneth Walker or Trent Williams, wait for that list, then decide.

Everything else, do now. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number tonight beats a hoped-for number on Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too — and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams pushes lines past the app's playable number.
items.takeaway: Wait only for inactives if your bet needs a questionable player — otherwise, if your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it now.
